items.title: Predict the Celtics win total this year (Staff Roundtable)
items.content:
BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - APRIL 28: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics celebrates a three point basket against the Philadelphia 76ers during the second quarter in Game Five of the First Round of the NBA Eastern Conference Playoff at TD Garden on April 28, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images	For the final roundtable, I asked the staff to come up with a wins prediction. We will all forget about this in the Fall, but as of today this is where we stand.

Ian Inangelo

Even without Brown, I think this Celtics team will have similar success to the team last season. This team is built to have success around Jayson Tatum who could put up a MVP level season next year. The depth around him is still the same minus Paul George who could see new life in a different situation and in a system that suits his skill sets better. We could also potentially see a leap from Pritchard and a bounce back from White which will make the offense even better. My final conclusion: 52 Wins.

Trevor Hass

The Celtics have eclipsed 50 wins each of the last five seasons, and that trend will continue this season. There’s no reason to think the number will increase or decrease significantly. I say they go down slightly from last year’s 56 and end up 53-29 to earn the No. 4 seed. If Paul George stays healthy and plays at a high level, I could see that number going up slightly.

Steve Hooper

The Eastern conference has leveled up in a big way. That means I don’t believe we will get near that 56 win mark again. I think 49 wins is about where I land right now.

Jake Issenberg

The Celtics have been a regular season wins machine under Joe Mazzulla. Never falling below 56 wins. I will say it again for those in the back. Last season the Celtics ranked second in the entire league in offense, while also ranking fifth in defense. The Celtics followed this up by addressing their glaring hole at back up big man by adding Mitchell Robinson, they get Jayson Tatum back, a guy who was selected to four straight 1st Team All NBA teams, and added Paul George who is still really good at basketball. To win in today’s league you need depth, defense, shooting, and top end talent. The Celtics tick every box. In last year’s Eastern Conference this team would have cracked 60 wins comfortably. Given the improved depth of the conference, I’m pegging this team for 57 wins.

Nate Moskowitz 

I’m predicting 58 wins. That feels slightly high as I type it, but I believe in the system to always stack wins in the regular season. Tatum is back with a healthy offseason. Robinson improves the big rotation. Hopefully you can get enough games out of Paul George, and when he’s out, internal development should help to improve on their record from last season.

items.title: Report: Kevin Love’s agent in contact with the 76ers
items.content:
LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 18: LeBron James #23 of the Los Angeles Lakers and Kevin Love #42 of the Utah Jazz talk before the game on November 18, 2025 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2025 NBAE (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images	The free agency dust is finally starting to settle in Sixers land after a blockbuster trade for Jaylen Brown and the signing of LeBron James. Thus far, the Sixers have signaled they’re heading into the season with their current group at 14 roster spots. Now, we’re getting an idea of what’s to come, with ESPN’s Dave McMenamin and other insiders reporting on the league’s top remaining free agents.

Per McMenamin, the Sixers “have been in contact” with Love’s agent, Jeff Schwartz, since signing James. He also shared that Love has interest in pairing with James, but has also maintained a strong relationship with Utah Jazz coach Will Hardy, with whom he played last season. As things stand currently, the Jazz roster is full.

The Sixers could bring Love aboard, albeit at a later date. They lack the cap space below the first apron to fill their 15th and final roster spot as currently constructed. However, they can sign Love to a prorated contract in mid-December without any roster turnover if they choose.

This isn’t the first time Love has had interest in joining the Sixers. In February of 2023, the Sixers were among the final two teams he decided between fresh off a buyout with the Cleveland Cavaliers. Love would go on to sign with the Miami Heat. He spent two and a half years there before being traded to Utah in 2025 in a multi-team deal that brought Norman Powell to Miami. Love spent all of last season with the rebuilding Utah Jazz, averaging 6.7 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.8 assists on 39.7 percent shooting and 37.3 percent from three in 16.6 minutes across 37 games. He started five games.

At age 37, Love’s best years are certainly behind him. However, you could argue that the Sixers could do worse with their final roster spot. Love can still shoot the three and is an effective rebounder (his per-36 rate was 12.6 rebounds per game). With the backup center spot occupied by Adem Bona and Ariel Hukporti, he’d bring a different skillset to the mix if the Sixers wanted floor spacing over rim protection and athleticism. By all accounts, he’s also a good presence in the locker room, beyond his relationship with James.

For now, it appears unlikely Love will join the Sixers due to roster and salary cap implications. However, there’s a chance we could see this move come to fruition mid-season as a straight-up signing or if the Sixers make another transaction within the next few months if Love remains unsigned.
